title: Define versioned typed Credential schema and compatibility parser
source_ranges: architecture-review.md ADR-S01 lines 21-43 (trusted identity/classification and root exclusion)
body:
## Outcome
Introduce a versioned logical Credential model independent of provider-native identity. Current evidence: no canonical schema exists in `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-secrets/src/lib.rs` (resolver-only contract, lines 1-28, 139-193) or its `Cargo.toml:1-12`.

## Deliverable and technical boundary
Define an opaque, stable logical ID that is never derived from path/name/native ID, a mutable canonical ref, schema/policy version, trusted-policy-derived class bound to provider/account/container/native IDs (never caller assertion or mutable sidecar), typed kind/ordered fields, `Observed` states (present/null/absent/redacted/inaccessible/unknown), tags, relationships, attachment refs, lifecycle/provenance, provider binding and opaque native fields/revision refs. Stable logical identity is an opaque ID independent of mutable path/name/native IDs. Root-private and recovery fields never enter ordinary resolver/cache/prefetch/equality-index handling; root authority is a separate interface. Support unknown types losslessly via versioned encrypted-envelope reference or explicit lossiness error. No provider calls, database, CLI tree, or migration of live data.

## Proposed owned files and interfaces
Proposed owned files: `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-secrets/src/model.rs` plus colocated schema/serialization tests. Keep types in the cohesive runtime crate unless measured dependency closure justifies extraction.

## Acceptance and oracle
Round-trip fixtures preserve schema versions, field ordering/type, exact native IDs and unknown fields. Parser distinguishes absent/null/empty/inaccessible. Redacted formatting and errors contain no known fixture secret. Unsupported future schema gets a typed error without dropping source data. Oracle: canonical fixture equality and explicit schema migration reference fixtures.

## Negative tests
Display-name/path collision does not merge logical IDs; BWS and Bitwarden Password Manager remain separate provider enum cases; unknown/adopted object cannot auto-replicate before reviewed classification; mutable sidecar/caller-supplied label cannot downgrade root scope; inaccessible field cannot be serialized as absent; attachment bytes never appear in metadata encoding.

## Dependencies / priority / lifecycle
Depends on ARCH-01 for shared runtime types and compatibility boundary. Medium (M), V2 foundation; High / intrinsic urgency 600; lifecycle Ready for synthetic fixtures. Blocks REC-01 and REC-02.

## Current evidence / safety
No canonical model, write path or `op`/`bw` adapter is in current V1. Work only in domain types/parser/tests under `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-secrets/**` or a reviewed shared crate. Synthetic data only; no provider tokens or vault reads.

## Rollback / recovery / open decisions
Keep V1 resolver types and behavior isolated; additive parser can be disabled before persistence. Unknown schema is retained/rejected, not destructively migrated. UUID encoding, exact field normalization registry and attachment storage are implementation-time decisions under review.

Lane/capability: code (proposed; confirm against current registry). Urgency is the intrinsic charter score, not the queue priority field or a dispatch instruction.

title: Add provider capability and scope descriptors with typed errors

## Outcome
Provide a small provider seam with explicit capabilities, configured scopes, atomicity and typed outcomes. Current V1 hardcodes broker/BWS and has no capability descriptors or write surface (`pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-secrets/src/lib.rs:139-193,493-604`).

## Deliverable and boundary
Define descriptors for supported/unsupported/unknown/not-authorized operations and fields; per adapter+operation declare deletion authority `read-visible-only|deletion-authoritative` and write guard `atomic-precondition|serialized-by-contract|unguarded`; until primary docs plus isolated tests prove otherwise BWS, `op` and `bw` are unguarded for writes. Consume the trusted root-scope/native-ID legacy exclusion contract owned by OPS-10/ROOT-09; do not create duplicate escrow logic. Include provider/version/scope/visibility evidence; pagination, size, native revision, attachments, auth scope and consistency. Define inventory/read/create/update adapter contracts, redacted errors and structured per-provider receipts. A Fleet lease/readback is not serialization; default unguarded conflict-sensitive changes are needs-review, additive create/history remains allowed. Implement fake providers only. BWS, `bw`, OP are distinct identities; no ambient authorization; caller/sidecar cannot downgrade root class.

## Proposed owned files and interfaces
Proposed owned files: `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-secrets/src/provider.rs`, redacted error/receipt module and fake-adapter conformance tests; preserve current resolver source files/default behavior.

## Acceptance and oracle
Fake adapters exercise each capability state; unknown/unsupported is never success; typed `403` is `PermissionDenied`, not not-found; truncated/malformed list is incomplete; revision/guard descriptor exposes non-atomic path; the descriptor is not a write precondition itself; unguarded conflict-sensitive apply defaults to needs-review, while additive create/history remains available. Receipt differentiates accepted, pending and readback-verified. Oracle: scripted fake responses and exact result-state assertions.

## Negative tests
BWS auth cannot construct `bw`; forbidden container cannot be read/written; synthetic root-archive fixture through original broker-compatible refresh/name fallback is rejected before cache/value return; missing attachment/field prevents “fully synced”; provider error detail and raw stdout/token are redacted; no generic delete method is callable in routine reconcile. A synthetic root-archive item sent through original broker-compatible refresh/name fallback is rejected before cache/value return; the actual legacy gate belongs to OPS-10/ROOT-09.

## Dependencies / priority / lifecycle
Depends ARCH-01 and SEC-02; blocks SEC-04/05/06 and REC-03. Medium (M), V2, High / intrinsic urgency 550. Backlog until model interface is settled.

## Current evidence / safe boundary
Current crate is a read-only resolver and `fleet secrets` exposes only `get|list`. Affected seam in `fleet-secrets`; all tests synthetic; no provider access or writes.

## Rollback / recovery / open decisions
Leave V1 default chain untouched and make new seam opt-in. On capability uncertainty fail closed and keep prior checkpoint. Exact SDK/API choice and per-provider auth mechanism await current official documentation and isolated tests.

title: Implement BWS adapter against explicit project scope
source_ranges: architecture-review.md ADR-S01 lines 30-43; proposals/generators-ops.json OPS-10; proposals/pki.json ROOT-09/ROOT-10
body:
## Outcome
Add explicit-scope BWS adapter while preserving existing machine-secret value and native ID semantics. Verified baseline currently invokes `bws secret list` then `bws secret get <id>` in `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-secrets/src/lib.rs:517-604`; broker also lists then fetches items (`pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue/src/secrets_broker.rs:190-266`). This is not `bw` access.

## Deliverable and boundary
Implement scoped list/read/create/update for one configured BWS project/machine identity; report granted scope/completeness and preserve native IDs, value, note/metadata and revision evidence. Root escrow containers/native IDs are deny-bound in trusted policy before any copy; ordinary legacy broker/runtime scope cannot read them, and root archives remain `ca-root` even when encrypted. ROOT-09/OPS-10 own the production activation boundary; this issue consumes that contract. Their completion is a production escrow precondition, not a blocker to fake-provider tests. Choose official Rust SDK only after current API/MSRV/lockfile compatibility is verified; CLI adapter must not pass secrets via argv or log stderr. No production inventory/mutation, project creation, or grant changes. Fake provider first; any disposable BWS test project is separately authorized.

## Proposed owned files and interfaces
Proposed owned files: `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-secrets/src/providers/bws.rs` and adapter tests; only touch `src/lib.rs` for explicit registration, no default-chain switch.

## Acceptance and oracle
Synthetic create/update/readback and list/get agree; stable native ID; pagination/scope status explicit; receipts distinguish accepted from verified; errors redacted; auth scope validated. Trusted root-container/native-ID exclusions are registered before escrow and ordinary legacy runtime principals cannot read that scope; root archives remain `ca-root` when encrypted. BWS remains unguarded for conflict-sensitive updates until documented and isolated-tested guard evidence exists; default update is needs-review, while additive create/history is allowed. Oracle: deterministic provider fixtures plus authorized isolated test project only if separately approved.

## Negative tests
Timeout, 401/403, rate limit, malformed/truncated page, bad native ID and missing item are not deletion; an unguarded stale update is not automatically applied; no secret values/tokens in logs; scope cannot expand from configured project; BWS token never authorizes `bw`; original broker-compatible refresh and name fallback reject a synthetic protected root item before caching/value return (no real project/grant changes).

## Dependencies / priority / lifecycle
Depends SEC-03. Medium (M), V2, Standard / urgency 1000; Backlog pending a scoped test environment.

## Rollback / recovery / open decision
Keep current fallback as default until behavior parity and benchmark evidence. If an outcome is ambiguous, reread by stable native ID before retry. Exact SDK vs CLI and capability guarantees remain open pending official docs and test. Production writes remain out of scope.

title: Implement typed inventory completeness and protected baseline records
source_ranges: architecture-review.md ADR-S02 lines 65-97 (verified-component advancement and no deletion from incomplete/inaccessible views)
review/architecture-challenge.md A-5 lines 153-165 (scope, grants, filters and cursor completeness); parent refinement 2026-11-12 on per-item ACL masking
body:
## Outcome
Represent exact scope inventory quality and protect last verified common baseline. Current V1 distinguishes malformed BWS list from absence (`fleet-secrets/src/lib.rs:554-604`) but has no cross-provider inventory or baseline; broker list handling is not reconciliation delete proof.

## Deliverable and boundary
Implement `Complete|Incomplete|Inaccessible|ScopeChanged|Unsupported` inventory result with pagination/cursor/scope/filter/field accessibility and `read-visible-only|deletion-authoritative` evidence. Add encrypted per-item verified-baseline components and a separate scope-watermark/checkpoint referencing exact `scope_epoch_id`, policy/schema/mapping versions and inventory manifest; each component preserves exact native revisions, readback proof and item cursor. Fully verified item components may advance independently; partial inventory/unresolved items keep the global watermark behind. Root-private/recovery values and equality tokens are excluded. Synthetic adapters only; no real inventory, database deployment or secret values in plaintext journal.

## Proposed owned files and interfaces
Proposed owned files: `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-secrets/src/admin/inventory.rs`, `baseline.rs`, encrypted-artifact boundary and fake inventory tests. Keep in cohesive crate/module until dependency evidence warrants a separate optional admin crate.

## Acceptance and oracle
Scope inventory is `Complete` only for all read-visible pages/required fields of the exact scope epoch; complete listing is not deletion authority. A fully reconciled item with both peer readbacks verified may atomically commit its own component despite another conflict, inaccessible item, or incomplete scope. Hidden/unverified items retain their prior base/cursor and record observed revisions. Any unresolved item or incomplete scope leaves the global watermark unchanged. Local per-item commit references exact scope epoch, policy/schema/mapping, encrypted content hash and durable event IDs; metadata remains redacted. Oracle: independent scope-completeness predicate plus per-item reference model.

## Negative tests
Same principal/account/config/token hash plus a per-item ACL shrink, two seemingly complete lists and 404 must become `MissingUnverifiable`: no tombstone, retirement, propagation or per-item baseline advance for that item; other verified items may checkpoint; global watermark stays unchanged. Deletion is confirmed only by documented/tested deletion-authoritative visibility plus in-scope permission evidence, provider-native deletion event, or explicit reviewed operator confirmation. Timeout, 403, truncated/malformed page, scope shrink, inaccessible attachment, cursor reset, or ACL-filtered omission never proves deletion or `Complete`; no plaintext value in journal/index. Do not invent ACL introspection APIs.

## Dependencies / priority / lifecycle
Depends SEC-02/03; blocks REC-02 and REC-06. Medium (M), V3 first, High / intrinsic urgency 650; Backlog.

## Rollback / recovery / open decision
No live baseline migration. Ignore unreferenced temp artifacts, retain prior checkpoint, retry incomplete observation. Select artifact atomic-write/fsync mechanism for target laptop and document its guarantee before production.

title: Persist append-only local journal and metadata-only outbox
source_ranges: architecture-review.md cross-cutting acceptance lines 218-238 (tamper-evident journal evidence limits)
body:
## Outcome
Create a durable local event journal and replayable metadata-only remote outbox. Current repo has general queue/outbox patterns but no secrets journal; secrets V1 explicitly persists no secret value (`fleet-secrets/src/lib.rs:15-28`).

## Deliverable and boundary
Append/fsync immutable schema-versioned events before effects; integrity chain, sequence and redaction class, with an independently protected monotonic head anchor if tail-rollback detection is claimed; exclude root-private/recovery values and equality tokens; outbox dedup by event ID and sink with receipt. SQL projection is secondary and contains metadata only; track remote projection state separately from local sync/baseline state. Under default local-journal durability policy, outbox lag may remain pending while a locally verified sync run completes; only an explicitly named remote-sink-required policy blocks run completion. Outbox lag never invalidates a verified local per-item baseline. Fake sink, local fixtures; no production DB deployment or live inventory.

## Proposed owned files and interfaces
Proposed owned files: `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-secrets/src/admin/journal.rs`, `outbox.rs`, schema fixtures and fake sink/replay tests; remote SQL deployment is excluded.

## Acceptance and oracle
Replayed duplicate deliveries are idempotent; event history never mutates; interrupted append detected and recovery is explicit; interior tamper is detected; suffix rollback is detected against an independently protected monotonic head anchor; state that compromise of journal plus anchor domain is outside the guarantee; remote sink outage never means sink-committed, but does not invalidate an already durable, readback-verified per-item baseline unless an explicit policy requires remote durability; journal write failure prevents external effect. Scan every output for fixture secrets, tokens, unkeyed low-entropy hashes; assert absent. Oracle: replay reference and redaction scanner.

## Negative tests
Malformed/corrupt event blocks replay; SQL ack cannot advance provider baseline; item paths/IDs are not metric labels; no plaintext secret or token reaches journal/index/log.

## Dependencies / priority / lifecycle
Depends SEC-02 and REC-01; needed by REC-05/07. Medium (M), V3, High / intrinsic urgency 600; Backlog.

## Rollback / recovery / open decision
Disable remote projection but preserve local journal. Restore/index rebuild replays immutable events. Hash chain alone cannot detect suffix rollback when the attacker can replace both journal and local head; require an independent anchor for that claim. It does not prove signer identity; separately decide whether signatures are needed and define signing-key custody before adding them.

Lane/capability: code (proposed; confirm against current registry). Urgency is the intrinsic charter score, not the queue priority field or a dispatch instruction.

title: Add authoritative deletion-candidate confirmation and scope-move handling
source_ranges: fleet_architecture_spec_v0_3.md §20.3 lines 1125-1134 (permission loss and incomplete scope are not deletion); current deletion visibility remains provider-specific/unverified

body:
## Outcome
Permit deletion classification only after complete same-scope evidence and confirmation. Existing BWS resolver treats malformed list as unavailable, not absent (`fleet-secrets/src/lib.rs:560-585`); no cross-provider deletion engine exists.

## Deliverable and boundary
Pure absence/deletion state machine uses prior verified binding, scope epoch, visibility/deletion-authority capability, permission evidence, provider-native deletion/trash/revision evidence where documented, or explicit reviewed operator confirmation. Distinguish `ObservedAbsent`, `MissingUnverifiable`, and `ConfirmedDeleted`; complete read-visible inventory alone is insufficient. Distinguish missing, moved, scope removed, revoked, inaccessible and unknown. It plans tombstone/history only; it does not physically delete.

## Proposed owned files and interfaces

Before proof, status is `ObservedAbsent` then `MissingUnverifiable`/`needs-review` if per-item visibility is ambiguous; only an explicit `ConfirmedDeleted` proof permits a tombstone/history plan; move preserves logical ID. Oracle: explicit state transition model; same principal/config/token hash plus ACL shrink, two apparently complete lists and 404 remains `MissingUnverifiable` with no retirement/tombstone/item-baseline advance, while unrelated verified items checkpoint and global watermark stays unchanged. When authoritative deletion proof exists, the normal tombstone/history saga remains available.

## Negative tests
Timeout, 403, rate limit, partial page, malformed response, cursor reset, narrower scope, outage, inaccessible attachment or per-item permission-filtered omission never mean confirmed deletion; reappearance is resurrection/new-generation conflict, not silent restoration.

Disable deletion classification and retain `unknown`; recover through complete authorized full scan plus review. A provider-native deletion feed can substitute for second scan only after version-specific semantics are verified. No live inventory without approval.

title: Add guarded apply, crash injection, and resumable item saga
body:
## Outcome
Apply only an immutable approved plan and recover safely at every crash boundary. Current implementation has no write/reconcile surface; source spec requires item-level saga, receipts and no cross-provider atomicity (`§§20.2-20.5`, `21.4`).

## Deliverable and boundary
Approval is bound to plan digest, exact scope, expiry and max changes. Durable operation journal precedes external effect; bounded concurrency and rate-limit-aware retry; unknown outcomes reconciled before retry; verification precedes checkpoint. Synthetic providers and crash injection only.

## Proposed owned files and interfaces
Proposed owned files: `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-secrets/src/admin/apply.rs`, `resume.rs`, deterministic fault-injection tests; CLI is a later wrapper, not embedded here.

## Acceptance and oracle
Model restart for 100 synthetic items with 99 reconciled/readback-verified and one conflict: 99 per-item baseline components remain committed and are not reapplied or given duplicate history; the conflicted item retains its old base and remains unresolved; global scope watermark is unchanged. Also inject crash before/after intent, accepted request with lost reply, partial history, active update/readback failure, journal/outbox/per-item-baseline commit. After resume, fake provider state and journal match reference saga model; no duplicate history, default unguarded conflict-sensitive apply, false success or watermark advance; named weaker policy is risk-labeled and not tested for impossible preservation. Changed revisions invalidate approval. Oracle: model-based crash-state oracle.

## Negative tests
`force` cannot bypass policy; non-idempotent unknown result is not retried blindly; required peer failure prevents completed run; no cross-store atomic claim; incomplete inventory or unresolved item does not advance global scope watermark; remote outbox lag does not roll back verified local item components.

## Dependencies / priority / lifecycle
Depends REC-01..06 and SEC-03. Large (L), V3, High / intrinsic urgency 600; Backlog.

## Rollback / recovery / open decision

title: Define full-scan versus incremental scheduling and checkpoint policy
stage: V3 operations after safe first-run cutover
body:
## Outcome
Provide reliable laptop daily execution only after safe initial migration and approved plan, with full scans periodically and incremental cursors as hints. Current repository has no secrets reconciliation schedule in V1. Root `AGENTS.md` requires the unified fleet schedule registry be updated in the same pass as any schedule change.

## Deliverable and boundary
Reusable CLI/library run contract, exact scope lock, persistent restart-after-sleep behavior, bounded retry, last-complete watermark and full-scan cadence. Timer invokes library; choose existing control plane/systemd only after repo conventions. No live schedule enablement in design pass.

## Proposed owned files and interfaces
Proposed owned files: `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-secrets/src/admin/schedule.rs`, target timer/unit only after owner selects surface, and schedule-registry update in the same implementation pass.

## Acceptance and oracle
Synthetic restart/resume retains last complete baseline; invalid cursor triggers full inventory; incomplete scope or unresolved item leaves global watermark unchanged; per-item verified baseline components persist independently; overlapping run prevented; stale lease does not take over unknown operation; tests never access real secrets. Oracle: scheduler/fake executor state assertions.

## Negative tests
Incomplete run cannot advance watermark; cursor-only absence cannot delete; no production timer before reviewed first-run migration, restore test and explicit approval.

## Dependencies / priority / lifecycle
Depends REC-01/07 and coordinate #9165. Medium (M), late V3, Standard / intrinsic urgency 1000; Backlog.

## Rollback / recovery / open decision
Disable timer, retain checkpoints/journal, run plan-only full scan when authorized. Daily time and schedule owner remain implementation/ops decision; update registry if actual schedule is created or changed.

Lane/capability: code (proposed; confirm against current registry). Urgency is the intrinsic charter score, not the queue priority field or a dispatch instruction.
